fixtures.which_table: Building-code table. The City's plumbing-code amendments delete the Uniform Plumbing Code's Sections 422.1 to 422.5 and Table 422.1 and send the count to the building code; the City's building-code amendments replace Table 2902.1 with a Southern Nevada table.

amendment.text: Toilet counts in Las Vegas come from the building code's table as replaced by the Southern Nevada amendments, not from the statewide plumbing-code table. For offices, restaurants and schools the replaced table has the same ratios as the model 2024 table: offices 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 after that (each sex); restaurants 1 per 75 men and 1 per 75 women; schools 1 per 50. New in the local table: a row for casino gaming areas, and footnote h, which lets urinals replace up to 67 percent of the required men's toilets in each toilet room in assembly and educational occupancies and up to 50 percent in all others. Urinals are not required. The total is divided in half by sex and fractions round up. Where a multi-user room serves all genders, the count is worked on 100 percent of the occupant load. Section 2902.2 (separate facilities) is not amended.
amendment.quote: [UPC amendments] Section 422.0. Delete Section 422.1 through 422.5 and Table 422.1 in their entirety and replace 422.1 to read as follows: 422.1 Fixture Count. Plumbing fixtures shall be provided for the type of occupancy and in the minimum number as required by the currently adopted Building Code. [IBC amendments] Table 2902.1. Replace IBC Table 2902.1 in its entirety with the following: ... Restaurants, banquet halls, and food courts (d): 1 per 75 [male], 1 per 75 [female] ... Casino gaming areas: 1 per 100 for the first 400 and 1 per 250 for the remainder exceeding 400 [male]; 1 per 50 for the first 400 and 1 per 150 for the remainder exceeding 400 [female] ... Business: Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, light industrial and similar uses: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50 ... Educational Facilities: 1 per 50 ... h. In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies.
amendment.rules_quote: [P] 2902.1.1 Fixture calculations. To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. To determine the required number of fixtures, the fixture ratio or ratios for each fixture type shall be applied to the occupant load of each sex in accordance with Table 2902.1. Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 2902.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. ... Exceptions: 1. The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicates a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex. 2. Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. In such multiple-user facilities, the required number of accessible fixtures shall be determined in accordance with IBC Section 1110.
amendment.separate_facilities_quote: [unamended 2024 International Building Code Section 2902.2, read on UpCodes' copy of the Nevada State Public Works adoption] Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer. ... Separate toilet facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by all persons regardless of sex and privacy is provided for water closets in accordance with Section 405.3.4 of the Uniform Plumbing Code and for urinals in accordance with Section 405.3.5 of the Uniform Plumbing Code.
amendment.kept_plumbing_sections: The City deletes only Sections 422.1 to 422.5, so Sections 422.6 and 422.7 of the 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code stay in force (text as quoted in the state pack from IAPMO's viewer: '422.7 Urinal Partitions. Each urinal shall be separated with walls or partitions to provide privacy.').

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 25/25 = 1 each. Urinals: not more than 50 percent of 1, so none.
50 each. 50/25 = 2 each. Urinals: up to 50 percent of 2 = 1.
100 each. First 50: 2; remaining 50 at 1 per 50: 1; 3 each. Urinals: up to 50 percent of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 each. First 50: 2; remaining 150 at 1 per 50: 3; 5 each. Urinals: up to 50 percent of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 each. 25/75 rounds up to 1. Urinals: not more than 67 percent of 1, so none.
100 each. 100/75 = 1.33, rounds up to 2. Urinals: up to 67 percent of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200/75 = 2.67, rounds up to 3. Urinals: up to 67 percent of 3 = 2.01, so 2.
100 each. 100/50 = 2. Urinals: up to 67 percent of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200/50 = 4. Urinals: up to 67 percent of 4 = 2.68, so 2.

restrooms_city.rule: The City's building-code amendments carry the state single-stall rule into the code: single-user and family or assisted-use toilet rooms count toward the required fixtures, 'may be labeled for use by any persons' with signs such as 'All-Gender Bathroom' or 'All-Accessible Bathroom', and must be as inclusive and accessible as possible to a person of any gender identity or expression (parent or guardian with a child, person with a disability with a caregiver). Shared all-gender rooms: the fixture count is taken on 100 percent of the occupant load. No separate City ordinance beyond these code amendments was found.
restrooms_city.quote: 2902.1.2 Fixtures in single-user toilet facilities and bathing rooms. The plumbing fixtures located in single-user toilet facilities and single-user rooms, including family or assisted-use toilet facilities and bathing rooms, shall contribute toward the total number of required plumbing fixtures for the building or tenant space. The number of fixtures in single-user toilet facilities, single-user bathing rooms and family or assisted-use toilet facilities shall be deducted proportionately from the required gender ratios of table 2902.1. Single-user toilet facilities and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet facilities and bathing rooms shall not be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of the sex, but may be labeled for use by any persons including without limitations "All-Gender Bathroom" or "All-Accessible Bathroom." ... 2902.1.2.1 Single-user Facility Use. Single-user toilet facilities and single-user rooms, including family or assisted-use toilet facilities and bathing rooms, shall be inclusive and accessible as possible to a person of any gender identity or expression, in accordance with NRS 651, including without limitation by allowing: 1. A parent or guardian of a child to enter the facility with the child; 2. A person with a disability to enter the facility with his or her caregiver; and 3. A person of any gender identity or expression to use the facility as needed. 2902.4 Signage. Required public toilet facilities shall be provided with signs that indicate whether the facility is to be used by males, by females, or by all persons regardless of sex. Single-user toilet facilities and single-user rooms, including family or assisted-use toilet facilities and bathing rooms shall be provided with signage as required by 2902.1.2.
restrooms_city.note: The amended sentence reads 'shall not be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of the sex, but may be labeled for use by any persons', which is hard to reconcile with the model code (which says such rooms 'shall be identified as being available for use by all persons') and with NRS 651.072. The page text states the state-law rule and the labels the City's text allows; ask Building & Safety how plan review reads the sentence. Also in the amendments: Section 1210.4 (baby changing table in new buildings with public restrooms, matching NRS 278.584).

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Las Vegas job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for the desert climate and see the rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Las Vegas hotels, casinos, restaurants and schools, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Las Vegas sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Las Vegas's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) used as an interior finish to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version, and ask the Las Vegas Building & Safety Division how it applies the rule to partitions.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Las Vegas requires a permit to alter a building unless the work is on its exempt list. The list covers "partitions that do not exceed 5 feet 9 inches in height" and "similar finish work" without naming toilet partitions, so ask the Las Vegas Building & Safety Division whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** in a business open to the public or a public building, Nevada law says a one-person restroom may not carry a men's or women's sign. Las Vegas's building rules let it be marked "All-Gender Bathroom" or "All-Accessible Bathroom" and count it toward the toilets the building needs. A parent with a child, a person with a caregiver and a person of any gender identity must be able to use it. For a shared all-gender room, the city counts toilets from the building's whole capacity instead of half for each sex, so ask the Las Vegas Building & Safety Division what it expects of the stalls. Nevada law bars discrimination in places open to the public on the ground of sex or gender identity or expression.
extra_rule_bullets: - **City or county:** these are the City of Las Vegas's rules. The city asks you to check that your address is inside the city limits before you apply for a permit, and its permit page links to a map that shows which building department covers an address.
page.confirm_office: the Las Vegas Building & Safety Division
page.stalls_intro: Las Vegas counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building. Urinals are optional: in each restroom they may replace up to two thirds of the required men's toilets in a restaurant or school and up to half in an office, and each urinal needs a privacy screen. An office with 25 or fewer people, or any building or tenant space with 15 or fewer, doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms. Casino gaming floors have their own count: one toilet per 100 men and one per 50 women for the first 400 of each.
page.install_rule: Only a Nevada licensed contractor may obtain a building permit for commercial construction in Las Vegas, and state-licensed contractors working in the city hold a city business license in the contractor category. Nevada requires a state contractor's license, and toilet partitions fall under the C-8 Glass and Glazing classification; only small repair jobs under $1,000 that need no permit are exempt. Confirm the classification with the Nevada State Contractors Board. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: The contractor needs a Nevada contractor's license and a Las Vegas business license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state, county, city and school district projects estimated at $100,000 or more, Nevada law requires at least the wage the state Labor Commissioner sets for the region each year from October 1. For a journeyman carpenter in the Clark County region that is $83.02 an hour, benefits included.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.375% in Las Vegas: the 6.85% statewide rate plus 1.525% in Clark County taxes.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hotels, casinos and convention venues:** finishes that match the property in guest-facing restrooms, HDPE or phenolic where crowds and round-the-clock cleaning are hard on stalls.

notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether a like-for-like replacement of toilet partitions needs a Las Vegas permit, and whether exempt item 4 ('partitions that do not exceed 5 feet 9 inches in height') covers toilet compartments (Building & Safety Division, 702-229-6251).

The Las Vegas Strip and much of the metro area are generally understood to lie outside the city limits, under Clark County or another city; this was not read on an official page, so the page only tells buyers to check the address. Clark County adopted the same Southern Nevada amendments (its plumbing amendments took effect January 11, 2026), but its permit rules and office differ.

The city's amended sentence on single-user restroom signs says such rooms 'shall not be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of the sex, but may be labeled for use by any persons'. The page gives the state-law rule (no men's or women's sign) and the labels the city allows; ask Building & Safety how plan review reads the sentence.

The rule on separate men's and women's rooms (offices of 25 or fewer, spaces of 15 or fewer) and the privacy rule for shared all-gender rooms come from the unamended 2024 building code, read on a secondary copy: check them in the code itself.
Las Vegas Municipal Code Title 16 on Municode could not be opened: read it once in a browser to confirm Ordinances 6910 and 6916 add no city-only change to the toilet table.

Public jobs: the Labor Commissioner publishes one all-in figure per craft ($83.02 for a journeyman carpenter). A partition installer may be classed as a glazier ($91.23) or sheet metal worker instead: ask the Labor Commissioner, 702-486-2650. Rates change each October 1.
Sales tax: the Department's component table is dated July 1, 2020; open the 8.375 Tax Rate Sheet in a browser before launch.

The city's access rules use the 2009 accessibility standard with local changes to the door of the ambulatory stall (the narrow accessible stall with grab bars on both sides); the standard itself was not read, so the page says nothing about it.
